title: Reported SNAP interruptions expose notice, time, paperwork, and interview route failures
source_unit: Urban Institute December 2024 Well-Being and Basic Needs Survey analysis of adults ages 18–64 in families receiving SNAP

denominator.unit: working-age adults ages 18–64 in families receiving SNAP; brief reports a nationally representative sample of more than 7,500 adults but does not disclose the exact analytic denominator for these published shares

observations.method: Urban Institute analysis of weighted December 2024 WBNS responses; respondents reported whether their or their family's SNAP benefits were stopped or interrupted during the year and whether the last event was involuntary.
observations.uncertainty: Retrospective self-report; exact analytic denominator and event duration are not disclosed in the brief. Reason categories are not mutually exclusive and do not establish agency fault, eligibility, or causal food-security effects.
observations.subgroup: Adults ages 18–64 in families receiving SNAP in the target period.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported interruption may reflect eligibility change, household choice not fully captured by the question, notice or paperwork failure, interview access, or another process; the survey does not verify the administrative case file.

denominator.unit: published subgroup target populations; exact analytic denominators not disclosed in the brief

observations.method: Published weighted subgroup estimates from the same WBNS analysis; subgroup contrasts retain the source's reference groups and significance notation in the detailed layer.
observations.uncertainty: Cross-sectional subgroup differences do not identify causal effects; age, work, children, certification length, income volatility, eligibility, notice reach, and documentation needs are correlated.
observations.subgroup: Age, children-in-family, and employment-status subgroups of working-age adults in SNAP families.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher interruption among workers or families with children may reflect schedule conflict, but may also reflect different certification periods, earnings reporting, case composition, or eligibility changes.

denominator.unit: respondents reporting benefit loss/interruption because they could not recertify on time

observations.method: Published weighted multiple-response estimates among the 182 respondents in the reason-specific subgroup.
observations.uncertainty: Small reason-specific subgroup; estimates are limited in precision, categories do not sum to 100, and reported reasons are not independently verified administrative events.
observations.subgroup: Working-age adults reporting a SNAP interruption because they could not recertify on time.
observations.counterinterpretation: The same interruption can involve several barriers; a reported notice or paperwork problem does not by itself establish whether the agency, household, channel, or deadline caused the failure.

observations.period: December 2024 survey; recertification difficulty and assistance

denominator.unit: published WBNS respondent universes for adults who recertified or whose families received SNAP in the prior 12 months; exact denominators not disclosed in the brief

observations.method: Published weighted WBNS estimates; help-source categories describe contact, not successful resolution or prevention of interruption.
observations.uncertainty: The source is retrospective and cross-sectional. It does not observe whether help changed the decision, amount, timing, interruption, appeal, or later security.
observations.subgroup: Adults who recertified or whose families received SNAP in the published item-specific prior-year universes.
observations.counterinterpretation: Seeking help may identify more difficult cases rather than represent a protective resource; the percentages cannot be read as success rates.

related_sources.claim: Urban brief summary and survey universe.
Administrative recertification timeliness context; different universe from WBNS.

boundary: This is a respondent-reported, retrospective interruption and route-burden layer. It does not link to administrative case files, identify exact notice or benefit dates, measure benefit amounts or gap days, verify agency responsibility, observe appeals/corrections, or estimate downstream food security, health, trust, political action, or return to SNAP. It is complementary to—not interchangeable with—the USDA/FNA state route-performance layer and SIPP transition layers.
